Theme Description: Focus on how the animals stand and move, and the proportions of their arms and legs. Captures observations about bipedal versus quadrupedal stance and detailed limb/foot morphology.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Identification of whether the dinosaur stands on two legs or four, including repeated confirmations of stance across examples.
Comparisons of arm and leg lengths, thickness, and overall proportions relative to body plan and balance.
Detailed attention to pedal and manual features including claws, hooks, toes, hooves, and overall foot shape.

Theme Description: Descriptions of head size and features, mouth shape and gape, and tooth form, often linked to potential feeding strategies.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Characterizations of mouth length, shape, beak-likeness, and how wide the mouth opens.
Observations of tooth size and implied biting/grinding functions, sometimes linked to weapons.
Attention to eyes, nostrils, jaws, and overall head size/visibility of structures.

Theme Description: Focus on the neck and tail as defining axial structures, including their length, curvature, thickness, and posture.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Notes on neck length, slenderness, and curvature, often tied to foraging reach.
Descriptions of tail length, thickness, curvature/arcing, straightness, and proportion to body.

Theme Description: Attention to colors, patterns, scales, and spiky dermal features, alongside uncertainty about color accuracy.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Green/brown palettes, striping, spotting, contrasting ventral outlines, and pattern distribution across the body.
Reports of dorsal spikes, spiky/rough textures, scales, and wrinkles along the body and tail.

Theme Description: General size estimations and body-build characterizations, from ‘lean’ to ‘fat,’ including elongated or wide body shapes.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Judgments of overall size ranging from small/medium to very large and shorter in length.
Descriptions of body slenderness/thickness, width, and overall elongation or proportion cues.

Theme Description: How the participant infers diet and function from morphology and behavior, including speculative functional roles for anatomical features.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Statements assigning herbivory or carnivory, sometimes linked to perceived speed or general impression.
Use of mouth/teeth, crests, neck length, hands, and spikes to infer feeding strategies or signaling/thermoregulation.

Theme Description: The participant’s analytic approach and noted ambiguities, including what features are prioritized and recognized knowledge limits.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: Declared focus on limbs or head and deprioritization of coloration, plus noticing unusual/obscure patterns.
Explicit statements of confusion, doubt, or evolutionary/relatedness uncertainty and novelty.

Theme Description: Links to prior knowledge and media, analogies to modern animals, and affective reactions of cuteness or scariness.

Subthemes.Subtheme Description: References to toys, movies, personal exposure (e.g., fossils), and perceived familiarity/unfamiliarity.
Comparisons to cows, alligators, raptors, deer, birds, horses, and feature-based relatedness cues.
Judgments of cuteness or scariness in the animals’ appearances.
